chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him)

about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'The Most Compassionate is firm on the Empyrean,' so he (peace be upon him) answered, 'He is equal with everything. Nothing is closer to Him than another. What is far is not far from Him, and what is close is not close to Him. He is equal in distance to everything.'

key_terms.الرَّحْمَنُ: The Most Compassionate, a divine name
key_terms.الْعَرْشِ: The Throne, symbol of divine authority

ai.seo_question: What does it mean for Allah to be 'firm on the Throne' (Istiwa) according to Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Tawhid, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the concept of Istiwa as a state of equality and transcendence rather than physical location, affirming that Allah is equidistant from all creation. This interpretation aligns with the Shia theological principle of *Tanzih* (divine transcendence), rejecting anthropomorphic notions of God occupying space. It serves as a foundational text for understanding how divine attributes can be affirmed without likening them to created beings.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 2. My father (RA) said: Sa`d ibn `Abd Allah said, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, on the authority of Safwan ibn Yahya, on the authority of `Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj that I asked Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS)

about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: The Most Compassionate is firm on the Empyrean, so he (AS) answered, “He is equal with everything. Nothing is closer to Him than another. What is far is not far from Him, and what is close is not close to Him. He is equal in distance to everything.”
